Script line 76 parses '^This reverts commit ([0-9a-f]+)\.$' from %b. Script line 88 uses exactly these; lines 86-87 compute (time - app_time)/60. Captured lead times (29.0 ... 173.0) match the dates in lines 49-60.

Table line 15: lead time 'tới commit deploy image đó lên production'; line 17: restore 'Từ commit deploy hỏng tới commit đưa production về một bản chạy tốt (revert hoặc bản sửa)'; lines 24-25: 'Commit git revert của một deploy đánh dấu deploy đó hỏng và là thời điểm khôi phục.' outputs/stage-4/scripts/devops/delivery-metrics.txt lines 17-20: 'deploys: 10, 0.8 a week' / 'lead time for changes, median: 51.5 hours (...)' / 'change failure rate: 2 of 10 deploys reverted, 20%' / 'time to restore, median: 117.5 minutes (each failed deploy: 45 190 minutes)'. Lesson output block matches the file line for line. Recomputed lead times and restores by hand from script lines 45-60: all match.

Script lines 90-91: 'median <numbers>: the middle one; for an even count, the mean of the two.' Sorted leads 22.0 22.5 24.5 28.0 29.0 74.0 ... give (29.0+74.0)/2 = 51.5; restores 45 190 give 117.5, matching the captured output. Lesson s5 now states the even-count rule.

Line 5: '[ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec .../lab-run.sh "$0" "$@"'; lab-run.sh ends 'exec docker compose exec -T lab bash ...'. Docker docs, compose exec: 'Execute a command in a running container'. So no cluster is needed, but the lab container must already be running; the claim's parenthesis says so, lesson s9 does not. Fixed dates: lines 7-9 'every commit id and every number below is the same on every run'.

issues.text: New in round 2, in changed text. 'the middle value' does not say the list must be sorted first. The printed lead times are not in order (29.0 24.5 74.0 ...), and 29.0 and 74.0 are not the two middle entries of that list, so I had to guess that sorting is the missing step before 51.5 made sense.
issues.quote: Lead time and restore time are reported as medians: the middle value, or with an even count, the mean of the two middle ones. So 29.0 and 74.0 give 51.5
issues.fix: Change 'the middle value' to 'the middle value once the numbers are sorted', or add 'sorted, the middle two lead times are 29.0 and 74.0'.
